rationale: The pain is real but mild — tracking parameters are a cosmetic annoyance for most users, not a workflow blocker that costs time or money. Privacy-tool buyers skew strongly toward free/open-source solutions (ClearURLs, uBlock, browser extensions), and there's no clear evidence that individual users or businesses budget for a paid clipboard cleaner; willingness to pay is the critical weakness. More importantly, the product is a native macOS app (Swift/AppKit), which sits outside what a Claude-based factory can build without a developer — the buildability score reflects this hard constraint.
solution_plan: This is not buildable by the factory as described. The existing product is a native Swift/AppKit macOS app — the factory cannot write, compile, or ship native Swift code. Even reframing it as a web-based link-cleaning API or browser extension runs into the same gap: the core clipboard-watching mechanic requires native OS integration that goes beyond Claude + a landing page + Stripe. A solo non-technical operator using this factory cannot realistically build or maintain this. If Youval were willing to license or white-label the existing open-source PlainLink engine, there might be a narrow path — but that is a partnership play, not a build play.
notes: buildability_with_ai fails the build gate (score 3 < floor 6). buyer_clarity also fails (score 4 < floor 6). willingness_to_pay fails (score 3 < floor 5). Product requires native macOS app development — outside factory tooling.
